content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To try some new tea, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Read the brewing instructions on the label (1 minute)
Step 2. Measure out the loose leaf tea (30 seconds)
Step 3. Pour the tea into a travel thermos (15 seconds)
Step 4. Add a drop of honey to the cup (20 seconds)
Step 5. Set out a tea tray (1 minute)
Step 6. Check the water level in the kettle (10 seconds)
Step 7. Place the tea leaves into the infuser (20 seconds)
Step 8. Warm the teapot with a little hot water (1 minute)
Step 9. Select the appropriate teapot for this variety (2 minutes)
Step 10. Clean the tea cups (3 minutes)
Step 11. Put away the tea tin (30 seconds)
Step 12. Locate the electric kettle (45 seconds)
Step 13. Find the sugar bowl (1 minute)
Step 14. Take a photo of the tea packaging (1 minute)
Step 15. Open the airtight seal on the tea bag (10 seconds)
Step 16. Clear off the kitchen counter (5 minutes)
Step 17. Set the table for tea service (4 minutes)
Step 18. Prepare a small plate of biscuits (2 minutes)
Step 19. Rinse the tea strainer (30 seconds)
Step 20. Empty the dishwasher to get clean spoons (10 minutes)
Step 21. Smell the dry tea leaves (15 seconds)
Step 22. Move the mail off the counter (2 minutes)
Step 23. Decide which coaster to use (30 seconds)
Step 24. Refill the sugar bowl (2 minutes)
Step 25. Research different tea varieties online (30 minutes)
Step 26. Browse a local tea shop's website (15 minutes)
Step 27. Check the expiration date on the milk (30 seconds)
Step 28. Iron a linen napkin (5 minutes)
Step 29. Listen for the kettle to whistle (5 minutes)
Step 30. Fill the kettle with fresh filtered water (1 minute)
Step 31. Plug in the kettle (5 seconds)
Step 32. Pour the hot water over the leaves (15 seconds)
Step 33. Find a comfortable chair (2 minutes)
Step 34. Turn on the kitchen light (2 seconds)
Step 35. Take the tea cups out of the cupboard (30 seconds)
Step 36. Set a timer for the steeping process (10 seconds)
Step 37. Get a spoon from the drawer (15 seconds)
Step 38. Place the cups on the saucers (20 seconds)
Step 39. Find the lid for the thermos (45 seconds)
Step 40. Pick out a snack to pair with the tea (3 minutes)
Step 41. Wait for the tea to steep (4 minutes)
Step 42. Set the kettle temperature to 175 degrees (10 seconds)
Step 43. Remove the infuser from the pot (10 seconds)
Step 44. Pour the brewed tea into the cup (20 seconds)
Step 45. Discard the used tea leaves (1 minute)
Step 46. Take the first sip of tea (5 seconds)
Step 47. Open the refrigerator (5 seconds)
Step 48. Fold the napkin neatly (30 seconds)
Step 49. Walk into the kitchen (10 seconds)
Step 50. Put a small spoon of sugar in the cup (15 seconds)
